Question: when was the last time you actually had an interesting game against Wager Master?

Answer: Three times today!

Screenshot_20220930-094034720×1600 111 KB

Starts with Who Are You Fighting, The New Deal, An Unwise Wager, and Playing Dice with the Cosmos, along with a Wageling or two. Unable to win by beating him up, the heroes beat themselves up instead to try and make Losing to the Odds an instant win when it appears. But then What Do You Really Know shows up, and across several turns the heroes get thrashed, until finally Idealist drops to 4 HP. Now Losing to the Odds shows up and kills her, and I don’t even bother trying to work around the impending Playing Dice trigger; I just fast forward so I can get my picture and try again.

Screenshot_20220930-140936720×1600 112 KB

This game started with similar cards on Wags’s side, but no Playing Dice this time. We did much better, and seemed poised to beat him this time…up until Harpy took the Unwise Wager (and unlike in past instances, this wasn’t due to the Ancient Tome issue, she actually did draw her entire deck because I didn’t notice what was happening in time to stop it). I’m sure there’s a story here…

Screenshot_20220930-170057720×1600 104 KB

Despite getting a reroll every time, Wags still had Who Are You Fighting, The New Deal, and An Unwise Wager at start of game! The heroes really struggled this time, with Wraith running multiple IREPs and Guise borrowing them to repeatedly hit Wags’s deck, all to ensure Playing Dice and What Do You Know didn’t see play. Wags was thrashed down to single digits while flipped, but got Who Are You Fighting back just in time to survive; the heroes then flailed helplessly, getting the snot kicked out of them by the New Deal while trying to come up with a plan. Iddy lost to the odds again due to her low HP, and the surviving heroes frantically scrambled to reshuffle their decks before an Unwise Wager could flip back up. But finally we managed to juggle Applied Numerology just right, reducing the New Deal damage for the two male heroes but not for the two women, so that we could finally make Wags be the one who Lost to the Odds.

Whew! That’s what you call earning a victory!

The_Justifier:

Question: when was the last time you actually had an interesting game against Wager Master?

Honestly, my table plays ol’ Wagey so few times that I can hardly remember any games against him.
I used to think he sucked, but the app has really helped me to understand how he’s actually meant to function, and I’ve had a lot more good experiences with him since.

fjur:

I may, from time to time, post a question in this thread if I have one

You get one magic spell, which you can cast once per day. What would you want it to do?

Alternatively, what spell effect would most match your personality, general identity, and/or characteristics, but might not necessarily be the spell that you’d most like?

And please try to avoid overpowered effects. Nothing godlike or on a world scale. (I’m looking at you, world peace spell.) And no infinities or absolutes.

Teleport. Even if it’s just line of sight, the ability to get from the base of a cliff to the top of it, without having to walk all the way around the hill to where it slopes and then slowly climb up it…there are perhaps better effects to have, but this is the one I’ve regularly wished for in my real life for years.

As to reflecting me personally, well you said I wasn’t allowed to godmod… but seriously, the power to conjure small objects out of nothing and then have them dissipate would solve so much of my clutter issue. “Where the heck is my can opener”, etc.

Manifest ten U.S. $100 bills. Enough to live on comfortably and give me the freedom not to need to commute and work many hours of the day.

I don’t know how involved the spell is, though. Is it a ritual that takes some time and sacrifice? If we’re just saying no strings I stick with my answer. Not trying to get too greedy, but it’s true when it’s said time is money.

Thunderbird:

it’s true when it’s said time is money.

So why not just wish for the power to create more time?

That sounds like god mode. Things start getting real weird when you mess with time. And odds are I’d screw it up somehow and have too much time with nothing to occupy it, or somehow short myself and just constantly be run ragged.

Thunderbird:

That sounds like god mode.

Valid; I don’t think a few extra hours in the day are unreasonable, but if you can do a five second ritual to step into Hammerspace for an hour, and there’s no restriction against doing it again when the hour is up, then that’s obviously an issue. There’d have to be some cost or limit to it.

Things start getting real weird when you mess with time.

Only really true if you can travel backwards in time (which would probably be impossible even with superpowers, just as making 2 plus 2 equal 5 is probably impossible even if you’re literally omnipotent). Time extension shouldn’t cause major problems as long as you set your various timepieces to account for it. Nothing about our lives would break if we all lived on Bajor and had a 26-hour day; at worst, one person having extremely high tier time extension would be able to break the economy, but only if that was what he actively tried to do.

And odds are I’d screw it up somehow and have too much time with nothing to occupy it

Not a problem I’ll ever have…at least as long as I have enough phone battery power to play Sentinels of the Multiverse: The Video Game! (I didn’t start this post intending it to be hamfisted product placement, but here we are.)

Teleportation and money-conjuring both sound pretty useful to me, although the latter seems fairly boring. I think I’d rather have a spell that would let me hire myself out.

The_Justifier:

you said I wasn’t allowed to godmod… but seriously, the power to conjure small objects out of nothing and then have them dissipate would solve so much of my clutter issue.

I think that that would be allowable.

Thunderbird:

I don’t know how involved the spell is, though. Is it a ritual that takes some time and sacrifice?

Not really, as far as I imagined it. I’m thinking that all the spell requires is an arcane word or phrase, a snap of the fingers or a series of gestures, or perhaps just a thought.

Yeah, I am of the opinion that messing with time is likely to be non-permissible. Although something small and simple like “Everything except for me pauses for an hour” might work, but not anything beyond that.

The_Justifier:

if you can do a five second ritual to step into Hammerspace for an hour, and there’s no restriction against doing it again when the hour is up, then that’s obviously an issue. There’d have to be some cost or limit to it.

Well, there is an inherent limitation in the spell that I laid out in the question:

fjur:

You get one magic spell, which you can cast once per day. [Emphasis added — Fjur]

Now, what would I reply to this question? Hmm . . . Perhaps some sort of telepathy spell? One that lets me establish a telepathic bond with someone for, say, ten minutes. While the bond lasts, we could instantly transmit knowledge to each other. This would useful both for teaching stuff to others, and learning things from them.

Alternatively, some sort of Multiversal Gate spell. Although that seems too powerful for comfort.

Or, as I a former Questioneer of the Day, perhaps I’d have a spell with which I could simply ask a single question, and a receive a mental answer to the best of the sum of humanity’s knowledge.

What’s a fan-created deck you wish existed?

I looked on BGG and while I didn’t exactly search exhaustively, I was surprised not to immediately find an EE conversion of Alpha. I had just assumed the community would have accomplished this by now. Doing the Terrorform and the Fey Court might take a while longer, and even Apex might have some balancing issues that would be hard to figure out, but nothing I saw in Alpha’s hero deck made her seem especially unusual, so I would think converting her from DE to EE rules would have been a simple matter of adjusting the math. I can’t do it myself, having never played DE and thus not knowing how to rebalance between the systems, but I would think someone would have…

Well, I think that the main reason a EE Alpha fan-deck doesn’t exist is this. One would have to buy Rook City Renegades in order to make such a deck, but then one would have DE Alpha and would no longer have any need to make a fan conversion. And I don’t think that anyone would buy RCR just to make that deck and play it with EE. That would be quite the monetary waste.

Just one.

Line break?

Which Sentinel Comics character would you want to have as a roommate?

Nobody remotely human, for certain. Maybe if Akash’Thriya was interested in seeing what more or less normal humans live like on a day to day basis, and didn’t accept superheroes’ definition of normalcy, she’d find me a useful object lesson. Probably put her back to wanting us exterminated within a week, but it might be a fun week for me, having her turn my laundry pile into a Primordial Seed.

Probably Haka for the delicious pies he bakes and the fact that he’s an all around nice guy.

Or the Scholar since John Rhodes abides and I assume that means I’d be living on a houseboat, which sounds about my speed these days.

Haka and the Scholar are both great answers, @Thunderbird.

I think that Unity and her bots would also be fun. Omnitron-X would definitely be interesting. So would Tempest, and I wouldn’t mind living at Plavu’Col. Being the Wraith’s “roommate” would most likely mean living someplace pretty swanky. Then again, living with any superhero would likely invite villain attacks, so maybe I’d choose Marty Adams.

What is one (or several) of your favourite flavour text quotes in Sentinels of the Multiverse (any edition)?

fjur:

What is one (or several) of your favourite flavour text quotes in Sentinels of the Multiverse (any edition)?

Without going and looking at any cards, my off-the-top-of-the-dome picks:

Legacy, Lead From The Front: “I’d rather follow a leader than follow orders” - Bunker

Argent Adept, Counterpoint Bulwark: “Once again, evil strives mindlessly for nothing.”

Unity, Brainstorm: “Most of the stuff I make up is way better than actual facts.”
(Unity in general is a quotes goldmine, I’m limiting myself to one per deck or I’d be here all day, so this one gets the absolute top slot.)

Kaargra Warfang, Orrim Hiveminded: “Hello, we are normal beings with skeletons, like you; let us share a welcoming hug!”

Deadline in the SOTM app: “It is with great regret that I destroy your civilization, humans. It is the only way.”

The Scholar, Flesh to Iron: “Show me your worst. I have weathered more than you can imagine.”
(Scholar is another of those heroes who I could quote half the cards in his deck in answer to this question, so again I’m limiting myself to the best one I can think of.)

Baron Blade in the app, versus Luminary - I can’t quote this one verbatim since it’s in the Baron’s usual pomposity, but the last part of the quote is “You dare impersonate the great Baron Blade!?”, which is just him in a nutshell, I love it.

Anyway, I’m not staying up for the next five hours to think of my top 600 quotes, this is just a random handful of tiles out of the scrabble bag of “top 1% of the top 1%” quality quotes from this amazing, amazing game. I know I mostly complain or nitpick, but that’s because I don’t have much to say about anything I feel positively about, beyond “I feel positively about this”; flaws and needed improvements actually require discussion, whereas “shared enthusiasm” is little better than duckspeak in my philosophy, and I don’t like to make the world any more Orwellian than it already is, just for the sake of something as minimally-relevant as people’s feelings (including my own).

My apologies for taking so long to get back to this; real life suddenly got unexpectedly busy.

@The_Justifier, several of those quotes I really like as well, particularly the ones from Lead From the Front, Counterpoint Bulwark, and Flesh to Iron.
